title: The Glass Eye
journal: Nesh-Deeka made me a Voh-Vastei of the Toh-Reel-Ka and gave me my first lead: someone in Gideon's market is selling an "Eye of Argonia". I'm to ride the rootworm from Helstrom's city tree to Gideon and find the dealer who sells it. Nesh-Deeka says Gideon's dealers tell the truth for a little persuasion or a few coins, and keep their papers in their pockets.
objectives: Find the dealer selling the Eye of Argonia in Gideon's market. (marker: Ovinius Calo, Rootworm Landing (Helstrom))

plan.going: I serve the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Xeech-Leel's secret warriors, as a Voh-Vastei. The Unbound want the Eye of Argonia, which lies at the Root; an "Eye of Argonia" is for sale in Gideon, and Nesh-Deeka wants to know if it is real.
plan.next: Ride the rootworm from Helstrom's city tree to Gideon and find the dealer in the market.
plan.ways: Ask the dealer about the Eye. He will tell the truth about it to a little persuasion (Speech) or for 20 gold; or his note can be lifted from his pocket (Pickpocket) and read.
terms: Gideon: journal 10: a city reached by the rootworm

answers: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka (rank Voh-Vastei) via Nesh-Deeka. Hist trees are sickening, the Unbound are draining sap, and the Eye of Argonia, a jewel at the Root, could heal all trees. The order wants it before Cuts-the-Old-Knot.
Go to Gideon market and find the dealer selling an Eye of Argonia; Ovinius Calo is marked and there is a Glass Eye thing here.
Talk to Ovinius Calo, persuade or pay him for the truth, or examine the Eye itself. I do not yet know if fighting is needed.
I do not know where the Root is exactly, nor if this Eye is real (it says Glass, so maybe fake). I can find out by asking the dealer.

title: The Glass Eye
journal: The Eye on Ovinius Calo's stall is glass. The smugglers who sold it to him keep the old silver setting it came in, at Gideon South Watch, a leaning tower south-east of the quay. I'm to take the setting from their locked chest in the tower's inner room. I may fight the smugglers or slip past them; the chest's lock can be picked, and their boss carries its key. A man called the Collector, an Imperial relic-hunter, has been asking after the Eye too.
objectives: Take the old silver setting from the smugglers' chest at Gideon South Watch. (marker: Smugglers' Chest, Smuggler Boss)

plan.going: The Eye in Gideon is glass. Its old silver setting, the only true part, is with the smugglers of the South Watch.
plan.next: Go to Gideon South Watch and take the setting from the smugglers' chest in the inner room.
plan.ways: Fight the smugglers (their boss carries the chest's key), or sneak past them and pick the chest's lock.
terms: Gideon South Watch: topic.mn06-persuade: a leaning Imperial watch-tower south-east of the quay
the Collector (Ennodius Vanin): Ovinius: an Imperial relic-hunter twenty years after the Eye; his note

answers: The Eye for sale is cheap glass garnet, not the real Eye. Its old silver setting went to smugglers who keep it to melt. Unbound and a Collector (Imperial relic-hunter) also asked after it. The setting may hold a clue to the real Eye.
Go to Gideon South Watch, a leaning tower south-east of the quay, and take the silver setting from the locked chest in the inner room.
Fight the smugglers, sneak past, pick the chest lock, or kill the boss for the key. As a fighter I favour fighting.
I do not know who the Collector is or why the setting matters; I may learn from the setting or the smugglers.

title: The Glass Eye
journal: I took the old silver setting from the smugglers' chest. Ennodius Vanin, the Collector, an Imperial relic-hunter who has chased the Eye for twenty years, had opened it before me and left a note: the setting is no use to him, but a ship's name is scratched inside the band. I'm to bring the setting to Nesh-Deeka in her house in Helstrom, by the rootworm from Gideon's Hist garden.
objectives: Bring the old silver setting to Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom. (marker: Nesh-Deeka)

plan.going: I have the setting. The Collector, a rival relic-hunter, got there first but left it; a ship's name is scratched inside it.
plan.next: Take the setting to Nesh-Deeka in her house in Helstrom.
plan.ways: The rootworm from Gideon's Hist garden back to Helstrom.

answers: I killed the smugglers and took the old silver setting. The Collector, Ennodius Vanin, a relic-hunter, opened the chest first and left a note: a ship name is scratched inside the band. That may lead to the real Eye.
Take the setting to Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom, by rootworm from Gideon Hist garden.
Go straight to Nesh-Deeka, or read the note and inspect the band first.
I do not know what ship it is or what the Collector wants; I can read the note and ask Nesh-Deeka.

title: The Glass Eye
journal: Nesh-Deeka read the name inside the setting: the Pale Harvest, a ship that sank in Hatandros Bight, the bay on the east coast south of Thorn, with a Gideon dealer's whole stock aboard. She already knew that two Unbound had asked after the glass Eye in Gideon a month ago. When I asked how she knew, she said "we listen" and spoke of the wreck instead. She paid me 100 gold.

plan.going: The setting points to the wreck of the Pale Harvest. Nesh-Deeka knows more than I told her of where the Unbound have been, and will not say how.
plan.next: MN07 starts; its first entry marks the wreck.
terms: the Pale Harvest: Nesh-Deeka: a ship that sank in Hatandros Bight with a Gideon dealer's stock
"we listen": Nesh-Deeka turns aside the question of how she knows

answers: The Eye in Gideon was glass. Its setting names the Pale Harvest, a Company freighter sunk in Hatandros Bight (east coast, south of Thorn) with a Gideon dealer stock aboard; the real Eye may have gone down with it. Nesh-Deeka paid me 100 gold. The quest is complete.
Nothing is set explicitly; the likely next step is the wreck in Hatandros Bight.
Ask Nesh-Deeka for more, or head for the Bight.
I do not know how the wreck can be reached, and I am uneasy that she knew about the Unbound and would not say how she knows ("we listen").
